| item | reading |
|:--|:--|
| Shape | Draft, base `main`, `Fixes #26181`, `patch` changeset for `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`. Not governed (0 of 11 paths), 770 changed lines. |
| Fix | Ruling `6429362190` letter A′. Every approval notification that names a record now goes through `notify({ about, text })`, and `subjectNamesFor` resolves the name per recipient. It reads the record under the system context, as the inbox does (#7497 ruling C), then picks the title as served to that recipient (`servedFields` over an envelope built by `resolveUserAuthzGrants` and `vetOrganizationClaim` in the request's organization). An empty title, an unreadable or masked title field, an unknown e-mail, or any failure gives the id. Recipients who read the same name share one emit, so no recipient gets another's title. The action-link pages keep label and id, with the dated #26181 note beside the #23594 comment. The templates keep `{{object}} {{record}}`. A sent-back note in the approver's own words still names no record. |
| Evidence | 38 check runs succeeded and 10 were expected skips on this head, 0 failed; mergeable `clean`. Tests (a)–(d) in `notification-subject-title-per-recipient.integration.test.ts` cover the ruling's four cases: a readable title, an empty title, an FLS-hidden or masked title, and two recipients with different FLS on one request. They are red on `main` for the title cases, and the FLS ablation is red. Package suite 1284/1284, derived gates 98 of 98 exit 0. |
| Carried | Claim surface, recorded here: `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` gains the per-recipient naming paragraph, because its `Deal D_123` example was made false by this change. Overlap: #26337 merge-tree clean; #26180 (same plugin) has no PR yet and re-measures against this one. |
